title: Learned immune phenotypes associate with lung cancer survival
summary: Unsupervised clustering identified two lung-adenocarcinoma immune-expression patterns, and a random forest assigned tumors in additional cohorts. The more immune-infiltrated pattern was associated with better overall survival, including in external gene-expression datasets. This observational classification does not establish treatment response or a causal protective effect of immune infiltration; immunotherapy outcomes were not available for validation.

source_review.scope: Primary relevant model Methods, Results and limitations; exact primary identity and current primary PubMed correction/retraction relationships checked.

evidence.tested: Expression-derived phenotypes in 514 TCGA tumors, with classifier assignment and survival comparisons in 1,063 GEO tumors and a 34-patient institutional cohort.
evidence.unknown: Prospective treatment-response utility and causal biology remain unestablished; immune-cell abundance is inferred from bulk expression and aggregate patient totals differ between the abstract and full text.
evidence.ai_role: Unsupervised clustering learns infiltration patterns and a random forest transfers those patterns to additional cohorts for clinical survival-association analysis.
